bib.title: Jev-Mem: System-One-Controlled Agentic Memory for Efficient AI Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Jev-Mem: System-One-Controlled Agentic Memory for Efficient AI Agents", Dongming Jiang, Yi Li, Bingzhe Li (corresponding author), UT Dallas. The text prints "arXiv:2609.23986v1 [cs.AI] 21 Sep 2026" and no venue, so treat it as a preprint. Code: github.com/libingzheren/Jev-Mem.

COVERAGE: All 64,554 chars read. That covers the main text (about chars 0 to 28,000), the references, Appendix A.1 (related work) and Appendix B (prompts). I did not run the figures script because the captions are in the text. Page numbers are not preserved in the extraction, so locations are given as section numbers.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Jev-Mem scores best overall on LoCoMo.
- number: 0.777 vs 0.700 for the strongest baseline (MAGMA), an 11.0% relative gain.
- setup: LoCoMo, LLM-as-a-Judge, gpt-4o-mini as answer LLM. Baselines are Full Context, A-MEM, MemoryOS, Nemori and MAGMA. One run is reported, with no seeds or confidence intervals.
- quote: "Jev-Mem achieves the highest overall LLM-as-a-Judge score of 0.777, compared with 0.700 for the strongest baseline, corresponding to an 11.0% relative improvement."
- where: Sec 4.2.

2. Memory construction is far faster.
- number: 158 s vs 1,044 s for the fastest competitor (Nemori), an 84.9% reduction or 6.6x speedup. A-MEM takes 3636 s, MemoryOS 3276 s, MAGMA 1404 s.
- setup: Table 2, total build time over the LoCoMo conversations. Hardware and the System-One backend are not stated.
- quote: "Its total memory build time is only 158 seconds, compared with 1,044 seconds for the fastest competing memory system, corresponding to an 84.9% reduction, or a 6.6 × speedup."
- where: Sec 4.3.
- note: the abstract says "6.6× speedup over the fastest competing memory system". By Table 2, MAGMA (1404 s) is not the fastest; Nemori is.

3. Query latency is lowest.
- number: 0.93 s vs 1.47 s (MAGMA), 1.74 s (Full Context), 2.26 s (A-MEM), 2.59 s (Nemori) and 32.68 s (MemoryOS).
- setup: average per-query time, retrieval plus answer, on LoCoMo.
- quote: "This is 36.7% lower than the fastest memory-based baseline at 1.47 seconds, and 46.6% lower than directly processing the full context at 1.74 seconds."
- where: Sec 4.3.
- quote: "MemoryOS requires 32.68 seconds per query, highlighting the substantial runtime overhead that memory management can introduce when complex processing remains on the retrieval path."

4. The largest gain is on adversarial questions.
- number: 0.962 vs 0.742 (MAGMA).
- setup: LoCoMo adversarial category.
- quote: "The largest gain appears in the Adversarial category, where Jev-Mem reaches 0.962, compared with 0.742 for the strongest baseline."
- where: Sec 4.2.
- Table 1 per-category scores for Jev-Mem vs MAGMA:
  - Multi-hop: 0.623 vs 0.528
  - Temporal: 0.637 vs 0.650
  - Open-domain: 0.618 vs 0.517
  - Single-hop: 0.802 vs 0.776
  - Adversarial: 0.962 vs 0.742
- Table 1 Full Context row: 0.481 overall, 0.205 adversarial. A-MEM overall is 0.580, MemoryOS 0.553, Nemori 0.590.
- quote (table row): "Jev-Mem 0.6230.6370.618 0.802 0.962 0.777"

5. Core design: a System-One controller makes the frequent, bounded memory decisions as typed probabilistic outputs (probabilities or a choice among options). Generation is not used for these. System Two (an LLM) only synthesises the final answer.
- number: none.
- setup: the controller is the proprietary "Jev" service (TypeSafe AI, 2026). Its model, size and training are not described.
- quote: "memory control itself can become a major source of latency and inference overhead."
- quote: "System Two performs the final synthesis over the selected evidence but is not involved in normal graph routing, candidate expansion, or stopping decisions."
- where: Sec 1, 3.3.
- Controller cost per operation is bounded: "A normal write requires one batched typing request and, when candidates exist, one batched relation request over at most Kw memory pairs. A query requires one routing request and, for each retrieval round, at most one evidence assessment and one batched candidate-scoring request." (Sec 3.3)

6. Write path (Sec 3.2, App B.2).
- Observations are never discarded. The quote below is Sec 3.2; App B.2 says "admission_enabled=false".
- quote: "The current design preserves observations rather than making an irreversible learned store-or-discard decision at ingestion time."
- Each node gets four overlapping type scores: episodic, semantic, procedural, preference.
- Candidates are found deterministically by vector, lexical, shared-entity and time signals, capped at 10 (B.2: "select at most 10 existing candidate memories").
- Jev judges only those pairs. Timestamps and exact shared IDs create temporal and entity edges without a model call.
- Semantic and causal edges are inserted at a threshold: "A returned relation score of at least 0.60 creates the corresponding typed edge."
- There are four relation views (semantic, temporal, causal, entity) over one set of nodes.
- Consolidation runs every 20 writes. It records decisions and links, and does not replace source memories. A System-Two summariser runs only if merge or promote has probability at least 0.85 and contradiction is below 0.85.

7. Read path is a closed loop: route, retrieve, assess, expand, reassess (Eq. 26, Sec 3.3, App B.4, B.5).
- Routing produces independent per-view need scores, plus multi-hop need and recency importance.
- A total graph-expansion budget of 80 is split across active views in proportion to need (B=80, gamma=1.0, minimum allocation 1 for views with need at least 0.10).
- Anchors come from vector and keyword rankings fused by reciprocal-rank fusion with kappa=60.
- Beam width is 10.
- Stopping rule: "Evidence-based stopping requires evidence_sufficient to be at least 0.95 and both missing_evidence and contradiction to be below 0.15. Retrieval can also terminate when continue_useful is below 0.15."
- Hard caps: depth 8, visited nodes 60, examined edges 2400, Jev attempts 16, 15 s retrieval time. "These limits can terminate retrieval even if evidence is incomplete".
- The candidate score combines embedding similarity, relevance, graph-need x relation usefulness, novelty, edge weight and support. A recency adjustment is added.

8. Gains are attributed to adaptive control, but this is not tested.
- quote: "the efficiency improvement does not come at the expense of reasoning quality."
- No ablation is reported (see LIMITS).

LIMITS
- There is no limitations section. The conclusion is only a few sentences.
- No ablations: no test of System-One vs LLM control, of each view, of the stopping rule or of the budget. The causal story is asserted, not shown.
- One benchmark and one answer model. Sec 4.1 says "two widely used benchmarks" but describes only LoCoMo, and the other is never reported. There is no LongMemEval result.
- Single run, with no variance or significance. The LLM-as-a-Judge judge model is not named.
- Baseline numbers may be copied from the MAGMA paper (same first author). The text does not say whether baselines were re-run on the same hardware, so the latency and build-time comparison conditions are unclear.
- The controller is a proprietary service (TypeSafe AI "Jev"). Its model, cost, hosting and training are unspecified. Timings depend on that service. Whether the System-One call cost is counted in latency is not stated.
- App B concedes that Jev scores "are not assumed to be calibrated probabilities".
- The time budget "is not a strict preemption guarantee".
- The System-One/System-Two link to human cognition is an analogy: "not as a claim that the underlying mechanisms correspond."
- The first author has other multi-relational memory papers (MAGMA, HAGE), so there is author overlap with the main baseline.

Text/table inconsistencies to flag when citing
- Sec 4.2 prose gives Multi-Hop 0.625, Open-Domain 0.610 and Single-Hop 0.797. Table 1 gives 0.623, 0.618 and 0.802.
- Prose says Jev-Mem "matches the best Temporal score of 0.650", but Table 1 shows 0.637 against MAGMA's 0.650.
- Prose says "best in five of the six categories". Table 1 has five categories plus Overall, and Jev-Mem is not best on Temporal.
- Prefer the Table 1 values.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- MAGMA (Jiang et al., 2026a): four-relation graph memory, the direct predecessor and the strongest baseline.
- HAGE (Jiang et al., 2026b).
- Evans 2008 (dual-process theory).
- Adaptive retrieval: Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2023), FLARE (Jiang et al., 2023), IRCoT (Trivedi et al., 2023), Adaptive-RAG (Jeong et al., 2024).
- Routing and cascading: FrugalGPT (Chen et al., 2024), RouteLLM (Ong et al., 2025), speculative decoding (Leviathan et al., 2023).
- Memory systems: MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023), Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023), A-MEM, Mem0, MemoryOS, Nemori, SimpleMem, LightMem, Zero-Mem (Xiao et al., 2026).
- Benchmarks and judging: LoCoMo (Maharana et al., 2024), LongMemEval, MemBench, MemoryAgentBench, LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al., 2023).
- Reciprocal-rank fusion is used but not credited in the text.

CODE
There is no code in the paper. These are the verbatim equations worth keeping:
- Memory loop (Sec 2.1): "Et =R(q t, Mt)", "ot =L(q t, Et)", "Mt+1 =U(M t, qt, ot)".
- Write path (Sec 3.2): "ot →type→candidates→relations→ M t".
- Read path (Sec 3.3): "route→retrieve→assess →expand→reassess".
- Prompt format (App B): a Noul holds an instruction plus true/false criteria and returns a value in [0,1]. A Choice picks one of keep_separate, merge, promote or uncertain.
- Example Noul, from B.4: "Instruction: Does candidates[0].content contain a fact needed to answer query? true: Direct answer evidence or a necessary intermediate fact. false: Only topic overlap or unrelated content."

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (Sec 1): "Workflow of agentic memory." It shows the loop of interaction, memory update, memory and retrieval plus reasoning, with the equations above. It is useful as a baseline diagram for a memory-OS note.
- Fig 2 (Sec 2.2): "Overview of Jev-Mem. A lightweight System-One control plane manages memory construction and adaptive retrieval, while System Two is reserved for complex reasoning and answer synthesis." It shows Write (typing, candidate search, relations, insert), the Memory Plane (shared vector and keyword index, four relation views, consolidation) and Retrieve (routing, anchors, evidence check, expansion, scoring, then System Two). It is the best single picture of the control/reasoning split.
- Tables 1 and 2 (Sec 4.2, 4.3) are the accuracy and efficiency comparisons. Table 2 is a quick, powerful display of the build-time and latency gaps.

PROBLEMS
- Page numbers are not available from the extraction.
- Table 1 bold markers fused numbers together ("0.5280.6500.517", "0.6230.6370.618"). I separated them by position.
- The ExpeL and Agent Workflow Memory citations print "(?)" in App A.1.
- Several references (Kang 2025a/b) are duplicated.
- The arXiv id 2609.23986 and the 2026 dates are as printed. I did not verify them externally.
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
